name: m1f
description: Read-only access to your own M1 net worth, positions, activity, tax documents, realized gains and queued trades, through the open-source m1f CLI.
long_description: Ask Claude about your M1 accounts: net worth and what you hold, what happened over a period (trades, deposits, dividends), which statements and tax forms exist, a year's realized gains, and what is queued to trade. Five read-only tools, m1_portfolio, m1_activity, m1_documents, m1_realized_gains and m1_trading; nothing can trade, transfer or change your account. The extension asks for no password: M1 sign-in is through a browser, so first install the m1f CLI and run `m1f auth login --browser` in a terminal. That stores the session in your OS keychain, and the bundled m1f reads it from there and refreshes it in place. On macOS the first call asks for keychain access; choose Always Allow. Unofficial; not affiliated with M1 Holdings.

tools.name: m1_portfolio
tools.description: Net worth, each account's total, and the positions held.

tools.name: m1_activity
tools.description: Activity over a date range: trades, deposits, withdrawals and dividends.

tools.name: m1_documents
tools.description: Statements and tax forms on file (listed, not downloaded).

tools.name: m1_realized_gains
tools.description: Closed tax lots sold in a date range, with totals by holding term.

tools.name: m1_trading
tools.description: Queued orders, auto-invest, the next trade window, cash to withdraw and pending transfers.
